phase: P0-W: Swift 6.4 cross-compile to Windows x86_64 from macOS

finding.ucrt: xwin takes the UCRT from the VS manifest's ucrt.msi: 'Universal CRT Headers Libraries and Sources' ProductVersion 10.0.26624 (SHA-256 prefix 54448641eef05831), the same for --manifest-version 16 and 17. Its MSI and 11 CABs contain no corecrt_math.h, corecrt_math_defines.h, stdnoreturn.h, stdalign.h or tgmath.h; its math.h (1,009 lines) includes only corecrt.h and carries the math declarations. xwin did not skip them.
finding.modulemap: Swift 6.4.0's Windows.sdk/usr/share/ucrt.modulemap (SHA-256 d704b35b343b9094829bd5b7ff134033c6cdeaf6188d7437f2955de9f842a200) names stdalign.h, stdnoreturn.h and corecrt_math.h, i.e. an older UCRT layout
finding.licence: a matching older UCRT would come from a standalone Windows SDK under separate terms; not downloaded

solution.patch: tools/crossplatform/windows/ucrt-26624.modulemap.patch removes the three modules in a copy of the SDK (math stays available through math.h, module C.math)
solution.toolset: MSVC 14.44.17.14 headers fail as modules (threads.h uses _UCRT_DISABLE_CLANG_WARNINGS from the UCRT; uchar.h then fails); MSVC 14.29.16.10 + Windows SDK 10.0.22621 (winsysroot-vs16 splat) compile
solution.link: swiftc passes lld-link no SDK library directories (only relative lib/amd64); -Xlinker -libpath for um/x86_64, ucrt/x86_64 and MSVC lib/x86_64 links. X5 is case-insensitive, so lib name casing is not an issue there

result.run: CrossOver Wine bottle ntsd-xplat-test (win10_64; test harness), with the Swift 6.4.0 runtime DLLs and MSVC runtime from the installer beside the exe
result.vsMacOS: identical except line 1 (os=other, clong=8 on macOS: LP64 vs LLP64); Windows stdout uses CRLF line endings

open: SwiftPM cross-builds of the package for Windows (a Swift SDK bundle with these flags)
